title: C. P. E. Bach’s Missing Symphony — public composition log
scope: The log the composing agent (Claude) kept while writing this work: the request, its progress messages, the commands it ran on the score and their output, draft publications and test results, up to the publication step. It was written during the work, entry by entry; it is not an automatic export of the whole session, and the same session composed other works whose entries are not included here.
policy: Messages and tool output are recorded as they occurred, shortened where marked. Private internal reasoning, credentials, access details, private paths and unrelated conversation are not included. Statements made during the work may be provisional or mistaken; later corrections remain in the log.

[A long batch brief was pasted: compose and publish one original symphony for each composer in the Missing Works catalogue who has no completed symphony, one composer at a time, claiming each open symphony request through the admin command, publishing live drafts early, testing every movement in the real browser player, writing a notebook and a public composition log, deploying an atomic release, and completing the request only after the public work is verified. Every work must be labelled an original AI-composed homage.]

NOW I know I said to do all composers, but how about we actually do half of the composers in each section? just to save some money.

entries.speaker: Claude
entries.text:
Composition brief — C. P. E. Bach’s Missing Symphony (work id cpe-bach-symphony-1)

Carl Philipp Emanuel Bach wrote about nineteen symphonies, among them the six for strings and the four “for twelve obbligato parts” of his Hamburg years: three movements played without a break, full of unison outbursts, sudden silences, abrupt changes of key and hushed, sighing answers. This is a new symphony in that manner, in A minor. No theme is taken from him.

Orchestra (10 staves, sounding pitch): 2 flutes, 2 oboes, bassoon, 2 natural horns in C, strings and harpsichord.

Movements (each leads into the next)
I. Allegro di molto, A minor, 4/4. A jagged theme for the whole orchestra in octaves that breaks off into silence; a hushed answer; tremolo outbursts; a tender second idea in C. The middle starts with the unison theme in D minor without preparation, climbs in sequence to a halt, and is interrupted by a strange calm in F major for flutes. Varied reprise; the end dissolves towards F.
II. Larghetto, F major, 3/4. Two flutes in thirds over hushed strings; a restless middle for strings that strays through flat keys; return; four bars that turn to the dominant of A minor.
III. Presto, A minor, 6/8. Two repeated halves: racing broken chords, unisons, a sudden quiet episode, scales in octaves to finish.

Target length about seven or eight minutes (his own run ten to twelve). Compromise known from the start: themes, unisons, the flute duet and every chord are written by hand; a program scores quiet and loud passages from the chord plan (accompaniment figures, tremolo, wind chords, horn notes, harpsichord).

entries.speaker: Score build and checks
entries.text: Build m1, m2, m3: write the score, check bar lengths, ranges, sustained notes and half-step clashes, validate with the site validator, compare with abcjs playback, and count parallel fifths/octaves between the outer voices. First build of all three movements, after fixing 13 parallel octaves/fifths between tune and bass (mostly where a broken chord in the Presto ended on the bass note of the next bar) and a missing natural sign in the Larghetto's last bars.

entries.speaker: Draft publication
entries.text:
Published live draft revision 1 with this public change note:
First draft of all three linked movements: the A minor Allegro di molto with its unison theme and hushed answers, the Larghetto for two flutes, and the Presto in 6/8. A revision pass follows.
